column1: # Podcast feed table - read by ytdlp (-t <table>).
# This is the sample. The real tables are one machine's library rather than
# code, so they live in data/podcasts/ and are not tracked; copy this file to
# data/podcasts/podcasts.tsv and edit it, or point -t at a copy anywhere else.
# One TAB-separated row per feed, six columns, empty ones included - a row with
# five tabs or seven is a fault, not a guess. Blank lines and # lines are
# ignored, so the grouping below is free to say what the rows have in common.
# A "#!" line is a directive about the whole table:
#   #!profile <name>  what these feeds are fetched as - one of:
#                     youtubeAudio youtubeVideo rssAudio rssVideo siteVideo
#                     Omitted means youtubeAudio.
#   #!jobs <n>        how many of them may be fetched at once, overriding what
#                     the profile alone allows (YouTube one feed, RSS ten).
# An unrecognised directive stops the run rather than being read as a comment.
# The columns:
#   active        1 downloads this feed, 0 leaves it alone. Pausing a podcast is
#                 this column, not a comment marker - a 0 row still shows up in
#                 a grep and in the count, and -a runs it anyway.
#   subdir        where its episodes go under ytdlp's <outputPath>. May
#                 contain yt-dlp output-template fields, e.g. a
#                 %(upload_date>%Y)s segment to get a folder per year.
#   nameTemplate  the file name in that folder. Empty means the shared default:
#                 %(upload_date)s %(title)s.%(ext)s
#                 Like subdir, it stays under <outputPath>: a leading / or a
#                 ".." anywhere in it is a fault.
#   playlistEnd   how many entries back to walk. Empty means 20, 0 means the
#                 whole feed.
#   extraArgs     yt-dlp arguments for this feed alone, on top of the ones every
#                 feed gets. Split on whitespace, and appended after the
#                 profile's - so a feed can override what the profile set.
#                 Not -o/--output, -P/--paths, --exec, --exec-before-download
#                 or --config-location: a row describes one feed, not where the
#                 run writes or what it runs.
#   url           the channel, playlist or feed.
#!profile youtubeAudio
# active
# The ordinary row: everything default but the folder and how far back to walk.
# A feed whose titles already carry their own dates, so the default prefix repeats them.
# A folder per year, and the whole feed: a back catalogue fetched once.
# One argument the rest of the table does not want: here the sponsor reads are the show.
# Paused: kept in the table, not downloaded.
